business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Item 1 Business, filed 2026-02-27)
business_model.claim: Pebblebrook Hotel Trust is an internally managed Maryland REIT that owns hotel properties and earns income by leasing them to its taxable REIT subsidiary (TRS) lessees, which in turn hire third-party management companies to operate the hotels.
quotes: Pebblebrook Hotel Trust is an internally managed hotel investment company, formed as a Maryland real estate investment trust in October 2009 to opportunistically acquire and invest in hotel properties located primarily in major United States cities and resort properties located near our primary target urban markets and select destination resort markets, with an emphasis on major gateway coastal markets.

our Operating Partnership and its subsidiaries lease the hotel properties to subsidiaries of Pebblebrook Hotel Lessee, Inc. (collectively with its subsidiaries, "PHL"), our taxable REIT subsidiary ("TRS"), which in turn engage third-party eligible independent contractors to manage the hotels.

business_model.claim: The portfolio focuses on upper-upscale, full-service branded and independent hotels in major U.S. gateway urban markets and destination resort markets, which the company believes generate higher risk-adjusted returns than other lodging sectors.

We believe that upper-upscale, full-service hotels and resorts and upscale hotels located in major U.S. urban, convention and drive-to and destination resort markets are likely to generate some of the most favorable risk-adjusted returns in the lodging industry over the long-term.

business_model.basis: Stated in P6 (8-K earnings release, Q3 2026)
business_model.claim: Operating leverage is a key margin driver: in Q3 2026, same-property total revenue grew 6.9% while total expenses grew only 4.0%, producing 58% EBITDA flow-through and 205 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion.
quotes: Strong Operating Leverage and Flow-Through: Same-Property Total Revenue +6.9% versus expense growth of just 4.0%, driving 58% EBITDA flow-through and 205 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion.
Same-Property Total Revenues increased 6.9%, well above the high end of the Company's outlook, while Same-Property Total Expenses rose just 4.0%, or 2.7% on a per-occupied-room basis.

business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Item 1, Tax Status) and P3 (10-K MD&A, Liquidity and Capital Resources)
business_model.claim: As a REIT, Pebblebrook must distribute at least 90% of its REIT taxable income to shareholders each year, limiting its ability to retain earnings for growth; it funds acquisitions, redevelopments, and debt repayment through external equity and debt issuances and property sales.
quotes: we are required to distribute at least 90 percent of our REIT taxable income (determined without regard to the deduction for dividends paid and excluding any net capital gains) each year to our shareholders and we generally expect to make distributions in excess of such amount.
As a result of this requirement, we cannot rely on retained earnings to fund long-term liquidity requirements such as hotel property acquisitions, redevelopments and repayments of long-term debt.

risks.claim: Pebblebrook cannot operate or manage its hotels due to REIT tax requirements and has no authority to direct daily operations such as room rates, making it wholly dependent on third-party management companies whose performance and alignment it cannot fully control.
quotes: We do not have the authority to require any hotel property to be operated in a particular manner or to govern any particular aspect of the daily operations of any hotel property (for example, setting room rates).
For the Company to maintain its qualification as a REIT under the Code, it cannot operate the hotels it owns.
